title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: we confess execution-order — Christ first proposed, then apprehended by faith, then justification, sanctification, glorification; mapping a distinct decree-series in God's mind overtrusts wit
pass_a_gloss: We confess therefore that God from eternity established that unto all to be saved Christ should first in place be proposed, then be apprehended by faith, thence that their justification should follow, then sanctification, and finally glorification: But if anyone by no means content with this order of execution should also wish to describe unto us a series of the Divine decrees, in the order of conception in the mind and will of God as it were distinct, and should urge with Arminius that the Divine justice is impugned unless this be considered as prior to that, he seems unto me to trust his own wit too much.
pass_b_english: So we confess that from eternity God established this for all who are to be saved: Christ first proposed, then apprehended by faith, then their justification, then sanctification, and at last glorification. But if anyone, not content with that order of execution, also wants to map for us a distinct series of divine decrees in the order of conception in God's mind and will, and with Arminius urges that divine justice is attacked unless one decree is set prior to the other — he seems to me to trust his own wit too much.
source_text: Fatemur igitur Deum ab aeterno constituisse ut omnibus salvandis Christus primo in loco proponeretur, dein per fidem apprehenderetur, hinc ut eorundem justificatio sequeretur, tum sanctificatio, et demum glorificatio: Sed si quis minime contentus hoc ordine exsecutionis, velit etiam nobis describere seriem decretorum Divinorum, ordine conceptionis in mente ac voluntate Dei quasi distinctam, atque urgeat cum Arminio, Divinam justitiam impugnari, nisi hoc consideretur ut illo prius, is mihi videtur nimium ingenio suo fidere.
